note: Hand-checked list. Every item links to its source. Add new items the same way.

min_wage.source: Florida Amendment 2 (2020) schedule, reported by FOX 35 Orlando and WKMG

events.title: Many people with felony convictions can vote again
events.detail: Amendment 4 restores voting rights after you finish every part of your sentence: prison, probation or parole, and all court fines, fees, and restitution. It does not cover murder or felony sexual offense convictions.
events.action: Not sure if you qualify? Ask the Florida Division of Elections for a free advisory opinion before you register.

events.title: You can pay for the train and bus by tapping a card or phone
events.detail: Tap a contactless bank card, Apple Pay, or Google Pay at the Metrorail gates, and on the reader when you board a Metrobus. A ride is $2.25, and you never pay more than $5.65 in one day.
events.action: Look for the wave symbol on your debit card. One card per person.

events.title: Florida's minimum wage started going up $1 every year
events.detail: It went from $8.65 to $10 an hour, then up $1 each September 30. Starting in 2027 it follows inflation.
events.action: If a job pays less than the minimum wage, that's against Florida law.

events.title: Old 3G cell phones stopped working
events.detail: Phone companies shut down 3G during 2022. Many older phones can't call, text, or even call 911 anymore.
events.action: If your old phone won't connect, it probably needs replacing. The federal Lifeline program can help pay for phone service.

events.title: Most bus routes changed
events.detail: The county redesigned the whole bus system for the first time in 40 years. Many routes got new numbers or new paths, some were cut, and frequent routes went from 5 to 19. Weekend service is now close to weekday service.
events.action: Don't trust an old route number. Check the 'My area' tab or the GO Miami-Dade Transit app.

events.title: Free MetroConnect rides fill gaps where buses were cut
events.detail: MetroConnect is a free shared ride you book on your phone. It covers the last stretch where a bus no longer goes.
events.action: Download the MetroConnect app or call 311 to ask if your street is in a service zone.

events.title: The Overtown Circulator bus is gone
events.detail: Route 211 Overtown Circulator was discontinued. The number 211 now belongs to a different bus, the Flagler MAX.
events.action: Use routes 2, 7, 9, or 77 instead, or book a free MetroConnect ride.

events.title: Overnight buses have new numbers
events.detail: The Night Owl is now route 401 (North Owl) and the Midnight Owl is now route 400 (South Owl). The paths are the same.
events.action: Working a night shift? Look for 400 and 401 at Government Center.

events.title: Little Havana Connection buses stayed the same
events.detail: Routes 207 and 208 kept the same path in the redesign. Route 8 on Calle Ocho was made longer, and the 8A branch was cut.
events.action: Routes 207 and 208 still link Little Havana with Downtown and Brickell.

events.title: You need a REAL ID to fly inside the U.S.
events.detail: A regular Florida license or ID without the star is no longer enough at airport security. A passport still works.
events.action: Bring proof of identity, Social Security number, and two proofs of address to a driver license office to get a REAL ID.

events.title: Florida's minimum wage reached $15 an hour
events.detail: This was the last $1 step. Tipped workers get at least $11.98 an hour in cash wages.
events.action: Check your pay stub. Anything under $15 an hour (for non-tipped work) is too low.
